source_review.notes: Checked IEC 61703:2016, IEC 61078:2016 and current IEC TC 56 dependability context; NIST repairable-system and HPP guidance; current NASA reliability/maintainability resources; and four NASA availability/maintainability publications. All ten final URLs returned HTTP 200. Formal measures, statistical models, agency practices and historical engineering guidance are distinguished.

evidence: Reviewed point and interval availability from state occupancy.
Reviewed alternating-renewal long-run availability and convention-specific MTBF/MTTR instance.
Reviewed two-state CTMC transient, steady-state and flow-balance equations.
Reviewed finite-state generator, stationary distribution and reward availability notation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The text distinguishes probability, fraction of observed time, event intensity, mean duration and capability reward.

evidence: Executed availability-two-state-fixture under python3 with exact output recorded in artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-064/report.json.
Recomputed mean uptime 50 h and restoration 2 h from intensities 0.02/h and 0.5/h.
Recomputed steady up/down probabilities 0.96153846 and 0.03846154.
Confirmed equilibrium failure/restoration flows both 0.01923077 per hour.
Recomputed initially-up availability at 10 h as 0.96175064 and separate observed operational ratio 1000/1050 = 0.95238095.
Recomputed exercise steady availability 0.95238095, transient 5 h about 0.969045 and balanced flow 0.00952381/h.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The observed ratio is explicitly not a sample from the synthetic CTMC and no confidence interval is claimed.

evidence: Confirmed renewal reward ratio requires compatible iid finite-mean uptime/downtime cycles.
Confirmed two-state stationary probabilities solve flow balance and sum to one.
Confirmed transient formula satisfies initial condition A(0)=1 and converges to steady availability.
Confirmed CTMC generator rows sum to zero and stationary reward aggregation follows state probabilities.
Confirmed operational downtime categories change the measure rather than contradicting inherent availability.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No renewal or Markov identity is applied universally to nonstationary, history-dependent, queued or policy-driven systems.

evidence: Challenged ambiguous capability, demand/window, planned/unplanned classification and denominator exclusions.
Reviewed inherent/achieved/operational clocks, overlapping phases, diagnosis, access, verification, authorization and restart.
Reviewed transient versus steady state, initial conditions, mission phases, scheduled/seasonal demand and maintenance cycles.
Reviewed degraded capacity, unsafe partial output, outage frequency, long-tail restoration and demand-weighted measures.
Reviewed finite crews/spares, queues, priorities, replenishment, stockout, shared maintenance and CCF.
Reviewed exponential/memoryless, HPP/ROCOF, aging/growth, nonrenewal, semi-Markov and simulation limitations.
Reviewed missing/ambiguous telemetry, censoring, classification gaming, fleet heterogeneity and policy transportability.
Reviewed all ten examples and five complete answers for assumptions, reasoning, limitations and bounded conclusions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Production availability requires domain, operations, maintainability/logistics, reliability/statistical, software/platform, workforce, inventory/queue, safety, configuration and decision-authority review.

evidence: Confirmed every claim binds capability, demand, time, configuration, environment and downtime policy.
Confirmed reliability, availability and maintainability remain distinct.
Confirmed means are accompanied by distribution/tail obligations.
Confirmed state/resource/dependency and scheduled-maintenance semantics remain explicit.
Confirmed model, stochastic, computational, empirical and decision validity are separate gates.
Confirmed no average compensates for an unacceptable single outage and prior baselines remain reconstructible.
invariant_checking.notes: The common mean ratio is consistently bounded to compatible long-run renewal definitions.

proof_review.notes: The chapter presents standard renewal and CTMC results but no theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: The fixture labels evidence synthetic_two_state_and_observed_counts_only.
Analytic and observed calculations are explicitly separated.
IEC/NIST/NASA sources are attributed with standard/publication status.
Simulation and observed uptime are not presented as validation by default.
No external review, operational prediction accuracy, distribution fit, future availability, safety or resource decision acceptance is claimed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Every percentage remains conditional on its capability, denominator, interval and evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked point/interval/steady availability, inherent/achieved/operational measures, uptime/downtime, MTBF/MTTF/MTTR ambiguity, maintainability, repair/occurrence intensity, degraded rewards and renewal/CTMC/semi-Markov/Petri/queue/simulation methods.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked capability/demand, clocks, categories, renewal and state construction, rewards, redundancy/restoration, finite resources, downtime decomposition, scheduled maintenance, observation, recurrence, tails, transient demand, metrics, uncertainty, structural/computational/empirical validation, trades and lifecycle evidence.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from availability semantics through simple formulas, multi-state operations and validation. Ten examples isolate recurrent errors; five complete solutions cover clock definitions, CTMC arithmetic, finite-resource states, claim audit and simulation lifecycle governance.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external IEC/NIST/NASA expert, reliability/availability statistician, maintainability/logistics or operations owner, inventory/queue/simulation specialist, software/platform operator, workforce/security authority, independent V&V, safety, contractual, technical-authority or resource-decision review is claimed.
